subject: Audit logs and data access evidence request
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fincobank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit logs and data access evidence request — post-call recap

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and our proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for the security review: 

Recap:
- You asked for evidence of who accessed customer data and when (audit log exports) to satisfy the internal audit / SOC2 review.
- Required timeframe: initial request is last 90 days, auditors may request additional history.
- Preferred export formats: CSV (preferred), JSONL acceptable; S3 signed-URL delivery works for large exports.
- PII concerns: you asked whether logs contain raw request/response payloads and what PII might appear.
- Retention & residency: you asked about configurable retention windows and whether logs can be stored in specific regions.

Questions / asks for FinCo to confirm: 
1) Confirm timeframe you want (90 days to start?) and whether you need rolling exports going forward (daily/weekly).
2) Do you need request/response bodies, or only metadata (event time, actor, action, resource, request_id, ip_address)?
3) Any mandatory fields your auditors need in the CSV schema?
4) Is S3 export (pre-signed URL) acceptable, or do you prefer a direct secure upload to a tenant-owned bucket?

What we can provide (high level):
- Audit events: event_time, actor_id, actor_type (service/user), action (read/write/export), resource_path, ip_address, user_agent, request_id, bytes_in, bytes_out.
- Export formats: CSV and JSONL exports; sample CSV attached on my side once internal team prepares it.
- Retention: default audit retention is 180 days, configurable per account up to 3650 days (multi-year) or down to 0 for ephemeral.
- PII: we do not persist customer request/response payloads in audit logs by default; we can provide hashed identifiers and optional PII redaction in exports.

Next steps (proposed):
- Confirm answers to the 4 questions above (timeline: please confirm by end of day tomorrow).
- Marissa will prepare a sample CSV export (last 30 days) and a short doc describing fields and semantics.
- If acceptable, we will deliver a 90-day export to a pre-signed S3 URL and a link to our evidence package.

Attachments: none attached to this message — we will attach a sample once ready.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fincobank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, FinCo Security <security@fincobank.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit logs and data access evidence request — post-call recap

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Timeframe: start with last 90 days. Auditors will likely ask for the 90-day export and a statement of retention policy.
- We need metadata plus the following additional fields if available: user_role, auth_method (API key / oauth / svc-account), and whether the actor was a human user vs. service.
- We DO NOT need full response payloads. We do need to know if any request/response bodies are ever captured in logs by default.
- Export delivery: pre-signed S3 URL is fine. For onboarding we will provide a temporary bucket; final delivery should be to our tenant-owned S3.

I've attached our security questionnaire to this thread — please have your security/infra team fill section 3 (logging & monitoring) where indicated.

Also: can you confirm if Redwood supports data residency for logs (i.e., logs stored only in us-west-2 vs. multi-region)? That is a requirement for a subset of our accounts.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Zhang
Manager, Information Security | FinCo Bank
alice.zhang@fincobank.com | +1 212-555-0199

Subject: Re: Audit logs and data access evidence request — sample export & details

Hi Alice — looping in details from our infra/security team and attaching a sample. 

Quick answers up front: 
- Timeframe: we can produce a one-time 90-day export and set up scheduled exports (daily or weekly) going forward.
- Fields included (sample CSV attached): event_time, request_id, actor_id, actor_type, user_role, auth_method, action, resource_path, ip_address, user_agent, bytes_in, bytes_out, region, tenant_id.
- Request/response bodies: by default we DO NOT store customer request/response payloads in audit logs; logs contain only metadata and identifiers. If a customer enables request capture for debugging, that is opt-in and flagged — not part of standard audit exports.
- PII: identifiers in logs are hashed/pseudonymized by default. We can produce either fully hashed identifiers or provide a mapping file under an agreed legal NDA if your auditors require identity resolution.
- Retention & residency: default retention is 180 days. Retention is configurable per-account from 0 to 3650 days. For data residency, we support region-scoped log storage (e.g., us-west-2 only). We can provide exports from a region-specific store.

Attachments included: 
- redwood-auditlogs-sample-20260618.csv (sample export, 30-day slice) — contains the headers and 50 sample rows (synthetic).
- Response: we will follow up with a short "evidence pack" that includes the export, a signed statement of retention policy, and the steps for an S3 handoff.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm acceptance of S3 pre-signed URL delivery for the 90-day export and confirm the destination bucket (or we can provide a tenant-owned lifecycle).
2) If the auditors need identity mappings, let us know and we will route that under the legal/infosec channel.
3) Jordan/Ben — I'll prepare the 90-day export once Alice confirms the delivery method and we have any extra required fields.

Thanks,
